A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entity-binding study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material reorganized between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original intervention experiments across nine language models and ten binding tasks, causal-model fitting results, and supplementary probing and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments using linguistic variations of the boxes and music tasks.

M1.justification: The positional, lexical and reflexive mechanisms, Gaussian-plus-one-hot mixture in Equation 2, and JSD fitting objective remain unchanged. Section 3.4 expands the presentation of pointer-validation experiments already documented in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: v2 adds a linguistic-variation scenario for the existing boxes and music tasks, evaluated on gemma-2-2b-it and qwen2.5-7b-it (Appendix D.4, Figure 21). This expands input-condition coverage while retaining the original task domains and model collection.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the positional one-hot baseline, oracle and one-hot positional variants, mechanism-subset ablations, and uniform baseline. Comparator membership is unchanged in v1 Figure 4/v2 Figure 5 and Tables 3–6.

E3.justification: The added linguistic-variation evaluation randomly selects a phrasing independently for each entity group from 12 alternatives per task. Existing layer-selection procedures, 150 interventions per index combination, 70/15/15 split, fitting settings and JSS/KL metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a robustness test asking whether the mechanism patterns persist under varied clause phrasing. The missing-entity, attention-knockout, mechanism-agreement and context-length analyses already existed in v1; their relocation and expanded explanation do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same confidence-interval reporting: below 0.02 for the main comparison and below 0.002 for the full and oracle models. No changed repeated-run counts, seed reporting or statistical estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 21 adds results showing the mechanism patterns persist under linguistic variation. Figure 2's right-hand plotted proportions also change slightly while preserving the trends. The main JSS comparison and Tables 3–6 remain unchanged, including full-model music-task JSS values of 0.95, 0.96 and 0.94.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the worked lexical-intervention example to retrieve ale from the original matrix G, replacing v1's inconsistent reference to G′. This repairs a localized mathematical example; the formal mechanism definitions and mixture equation are unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: three interacting retrieval mechanisms, weakened positional retrieval in middle groups, validation across nine models and ten tasks, and approximately 95% distributional agreement.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the linguistic-variation results as extending applicability beyond fixed clause templates (Section 5 and Appendix D.4). The pointer interpretation, suppression-confound argument and proposed connection to lost-in-the-middle behavior were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly states entity-set sizes of 23–80, explicitly clarifies full residual-vector patching, and documents randomized phrasing construction. Table 1 corrects inconsistent examples. Training hyperparameters and code/data access remain unchanged, while v1's brief disclosure of LLM assistance with helper functions is removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including the critique of positional-only accounts and the connection to prior causal-model combination work. Citation formatting and relocated discussions do not alter this relationship.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the appendices into thematic sections covering generalization, positional encoding, entity-token signals, additional experiments and causal models. It also introduces a dedicated main-text Section 3.4 explaining reflexive validation, revises surrounding explanations and cross-references, and updates the publication header.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel reflexive-validation display (Figure 4), a pointer schematic (Figure 7), and linguistic-variation plots (Figure 21). Figures 1–3 receive caption or axis-label refinements, and appendix displays are rearranged. Most existing graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The linguistic-variation experiment adds useful robustness evidence, while the dedicated reflexive-validation explanation, schematic and corrected examples improve clarity. v1 already contained the decisive pointer controls and unchanged headline results, limiting the overall gain. These benefits outweigh the small loss of implementation-provenance detail from removing the LLM-use disclosure.
